description: Every DNSFilter API operation, plus one-command answers to 'why is this site blocked for this client' and 'which clients are behind on the roaming agent'.

novel_features.name: Why is this site blocked
novel_features.description: Name the site or roaming-client policy and rule that blocks or allows a domain for a client org, plus query-log hits. Does not evaluate user, collection, LAN-subnet, Universal List or AppAware rules.

novel_features.name: Allow it for this client
novel_features.description: Add a domain to the allow list of the policies blocking it for a client (from the query log, else the assigned site or roaming-client policies that block it). Previews by default; --confirm --note writes, then reads back.

novel_features.name: Unblock request triage
novel_features.description: Review pending end-user unblock requests grouped by domain across every client, with threat flags, age, and DNSFilter's own already-covered check. Needs unblock requests enabled on the account.

novel_features.name: Roaming client version drift
novel_features.description: See which client orgs have roaming clients behind the latest agent release, or on a specific bad build, with auto-update state per org. Joins the synced fleet with the vendor's live release feed.

novel_features.name: Silent or unprotected roaming clients
novel_features.description: List roaming clients that stopped checking in or are unprotected, bypassed or of unknown protection state, grouped by client org with age buckets. Reads the local mirror; sync first.

novel_features.name: Which clients allow or block a domain
novel_features.description: Find every policy across every client whose allow or block list holds a domain or a parent domain, with counts of the sites and roaming clients it governs. Reads the local mirror; sync first.

novel_features.name: Policy security audit
novel_features.description: Flag allow-listed domains now categorized as threats, unblocked security categories, and allowed unknown domains; with --baseline <policy-id>, also drift from that baseline policy.
